newsitem.title: GUINEA: Exiled leader Momoh back in Sierra Leone Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Exiled leader Momoh back in Sierra Leone Sunday.

text.p: Sierra Leone's deposed president Joseph Momoh said on Friday he was returning home this weekend after living in exile in neighbouring Guinea since the army toppled his elected government in 1992.
Momoh told Reuters in an interview in the Guinean capital the Sierra Leone government now headed by civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah had cleared the way for his homecoming.

A retired general and former defence minister, Momoh will live in a government house, draw a monthly pension of 900,000 Leones ($900) and be provided with a chauffeur-driven car, servants and security guards.
"I am going home with lots of fond memories for the entire people of Guinea and my friends in Conakry and most especially my brother and friend General Lansana Conte (the president)," Momoh said.
Momoh and his family fled to Guinea as young officers seized power in April 1992 accusing him of neglecting the army in the face of a rebel campaign.
He hardly left Conakry during his exile, spending most of the time reading, playing tennis, learning French or writing his memoires.
Asked if he still nursed political ambition, he said: "Time will tell."
He hailed the peace accord signed in Ivory Coast last November 30 ending the war started in 1991 by United Revolutionary Front rebels accusing him of unjust rule.
"I personally congratulated President Kabbah. I only hope this is lasting peace as we badly need to reconstruct the war-devastated country," he said.
He lauded Kabbah, who came to power after elections last March ending four years of army rule.
"I have him in the highest esteem -- a fine gentleman I would be willing to cooperate with in any field that would spell progress for our nation," Momoh added.
